Hunter Aircrafts 
*323. SHRI C. M. IBRAHIM: Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether the 'Hunter' a veteran aircraft of 1971 Indo-Pak War, made its last 
flight at the Air Force Day Parade 2001; 
(b) if so, how many Hunters had been grounded that day; and 
(c) the aircraft that is expected to take over the role of the 'Hunter' in the 
Air Force Fleet? 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERN ANDES): (a) to 
(c) The Hunter aircraft made its last flight on 8th October, 2001 (Air Force 
Day) when it was ceremoniously phased out during the Air Force Day 
Parade at the Air Force Station, Palam. 
A total of eight Hunter air crafts were phased out on 8th October, 2001. With 
that all Hunter aircrafts were phased out of service. 
Another suitable aircraft has been assigned the role of Hunter in the Indian 
Air Force. However, details cannot be divulged due to reasons of national 
security. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA       [12 December, 2001] 
Activities of Lashkar-e-Toiba in India 
*324. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY : Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it has come to the Government's notice that Pakistan-based terrorist 
organisation, Lashkar-e-Toiba (L-e-T) is functioning in more than 36 cities in India, 
backing organised criminal gangs and is involved in large scale drug trafficking and 
smuggling of counterfeit Indian currency; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) what steps have been taken so far to smash the disruptive activities of 
L-e-T and similar terrorist outfits operating in this country and with what 
results? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN TH E MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO): (a) and (b) Lashkar-e-
Toiba is mainly operating in Jammu and Kashmir, but there are reports that the 
outfit has spread its network in other parts of the country as well like 
Hyderabad, Mumbai, Jodhpur, Kanpur, Dehradun, Bhuj and Delhi. No confirmed 
report of LeT's involvement in drug trafficking and smuggling of counterfeit Indian 
currency has been received. However, such possibilities cannot be ruled out. 
(c) Government has adopted a well coordinated and multi-pronged approach for 
tackling the activities of militants which includes strengthening the border 
management to check illegal cross border activities, gearing up the intelligence 
machinery, close interaction between agencies of the Centre and the State 
Governments, neutralizing plans of militants and anti-national elements by 
coordinated action, modernization and upgradation of police and security forces 
with advanced sophisticated weapons and communication system, etc. As a 
result of coordinated action, several terrorist modules have been neutralized. 
Diplomatic initiatives have also been taken with various countries to enlist 
their support in countering the activities of militant groups. 
6 

[12 December, 2001]      RAJYA SABHA 
Prevention of Terrorism Ordinance, 2001 has been promulgated under 
which 25 organisations, including Lashkar-e-Toiba have been notified as 
Terrorist Organisations.

IPS Officer held in Dowry Case 
*331. SHRI KHAGEN DAS: Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the news-item 
titled "IPS officer held for demanding Rs. 5 crore dowry" appearing in the

(b) whether the alleged officer has since been suspended from 
11 

RAJYA SABHA       [12 December, 2001] 
service; and 
(c) what steps have been taken to ensure that the officer does not use his 
influence in the matter? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The IPS officer in question , who belongs to Madhya Pradesh cadre,

State Government of Madhya Pradesh is competent to proceed against the officer 
since he is presently serving in connection with the affairs of that State. It is also 
for the State Government to ensure that the officer is not able to influence or 
interfere with the investigation of the case.

Naval Base Project Seabird, Karnataka 
*334. SHRI K.V. KRISHNAMURTHY:  Will the Minister of DEFENCE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the new naval base Project Seabird near Karwar (Karnataka) 
was envisaged in the Naval Plan 1980—55 to be completed by 1995; 
(b) whether the original project outlay of  Rs. 350 crore in 1985 escalated 
to Rs. 1295 crore in 1995, despite reduction in scope by more than 50 per 
cent; and 
(c) whether the rehabilitation package fo r the displaced families is in 
place and if so, when the project is likely to be commissioned? 
14 

[12 December, 2001]      RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERN ANDES): (a) to 
(c) In August 1985 the Ministry of Defence approved the construction of a 
Naval Base at Karwar at an initial estimated expenditure of Rs. 350.00 crores. 
The initial estimates were indicative and were made without a Master Plan 
and a Detailed Project Report. The scope of work, different Sub components 
of the Dockyard and details regarding supporting Infrastructure had not been 
worked out. In the year 1989 a Consultant was appointed to draw the Master 
Plan and detailed Project report for Phase-1-A and 1-B of the Project. The 
Consultant submitted his report in 1990. However, the Project could not 
progress further due to financial constraints. Based on the Final Project 
Report, with reduced scope of Phase-I, when compared with the initial 
proposal and keeping in view the escalation of price level in the meantime, the 
Ministry of Defence finally approved in October 1995 the construction of 
Phase-I of the Project at a projected cost of Rs. 1294.41 crores. 
The rehabilitation package finalized  in consultation with the State 
Government, included interalia, a cash allowance and a house site, education 
stipend, and relief for food and medicines. The rehabilitation Project has 
been finalized at a total amount of Rs. 126.96 crores and State Government 
of Karnataka has already been paid a sum of Rs. 117.02 crores. The Balance 
amount will be paid on Audit of accounts. 
The Project is scheduled to be completed by 2005.

2446. DR. KARAN SINGH: Will the Minister of DEFENCE be

(c) what were the precise functions of TA as envisaged at that time; and 
how far they have been watered down? 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES): (a) 
and (b) Yes, Sir. Territorial Army (TA) and some units of Navy and Air Force 
similar to TA were in existence at 
45 

RAJYA SABHA       [12 December, 2001] 
the time of Independence. In 1949, the projected strength of the Territorial 
Army alone was 1.3 lakhs. Over the years, the territorial equivalents of the 
Navy and Air Force have ceased to exist and some of the Territorial Army 
units have been converted to regular army units. The current strength of the 
Territorial Army stands at 32,200 personnel. 
(c) The role and function of Territorial Army, in 1951, included: (i) 
relieve the regular army of static duties; (ii) provide coastal defence 
and anti-aircraft units; (iii) provide field formations and units for the 
regular army, as and when required. 
These functions have undergone certain modifications over the years to 
suit the changinng internal and external security environment. The present 
functions of the force include carrying out static security duties, internal 
security duties and aid to civil authorities, as and when required.

2473. SHRI ANANTRAY DEVSHANKER  DAVE: Will the Minister of

64 

[12 December, 2001]       RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI GEORGE FERNANDES): (a) to 
(d) The Following arrangements exist for giving warning signals to 
fishermen: 
(i) Weather bulletins including cyclone warning for fishermen are 
broadcast on AIR. 
(ii) Storm warning signals in the form of flags/lights are displayed at 
all ports. 
(iii) Related State Government Departments are informed of impending 
danger at sea so that they can also inform the fishermen. 
(iv) In addition, regular instructional lectures are organised by Coast Guard to 
indicate maritime boundaries and safety precautions. 
Fishermen being apprehended by Pakistan cannot be attributed to failure on the 
Part of Coast Guard as despite advice they do not keep within national maritime 
boundaries. It has been found that fishermen's boats are not properly equipped 
with communication and navigational equipment. In addition, some fishermen 
continue to disregard the advice given by Coast Guard and get apprehended by 
Pakistan Maritime Security Agency (MSA). 
Fishing in territorial waters (Up to 12 nautical mile) is a state subject and 
the operations of fishermen are governed by Marine Fisheries Regulation Act of 
the respective coastal states. The Un ion Government is responsible for 
administering operations of fishermen in deep sea (beyond 12 nautical miles and 
up to 200 nautical miles). 
Coast Guard has recommended to State Governments to equip fishing vessels 
with basic radio communication equipment. The Union Ministry of Agriculture is 
examining a proposal of establishing satellite based Vessel Management 
System for fishing vessels.

Pakistani National Getting Indian Identity Proofs 
2508. SHRI RAMACHANDRA KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have prepared an action plan to keep a watch on the 
large number of Pakistani Nationals, who visits the country on short term basis 
and later acquire Indian identity by acquiring ration cards and passports and are 
helping anti-national elements; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps taken/proposed to be taken by Government to tighten the 
verification system for issue of driving license, identity cards etc. so that 
foreigners are not able to assume a local identity? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI CHENNAMANENI VIDYA SAGAR RAO): (a) to (c) In order to 
keep a close watch on the Pak Nationals visiting India on short-term visa, the 
following procedure has been prescribed: 
1. The visa applications are received in quadruplicate; 
2. The visa is given for a specified city/town and the visa holder is not 
allowed to visit any other place without seeking prior permission; 
3. One copy of the application form is given to the visa holder, one is 
retained by the Mission, one is sent to the Superintendent of Police of the 
first place to be visited by the visa holder and one copy is sent to the 
Revenue Intelligence; 
94 

[12 December, 2001]      RAJYA SABHA 
4. The visa holder hands over his copy of the application to the Immigration 
Officer at the checkpost of entry; 
5. A temporary permit is issued to him (if his stay is more than 14 days) and 
copies of this are sent to all the Superintendents of Police of the places to 
be visited by the Pak visa holder; 
6. Pak visa holder is required to report to the SP of the place of his first visit 
and subsequent places of visit within 24 hrs where he is given a regular 
residential permit specifying the permitted period of his stay. The Pak visa 
holder is required to intimate his intended departure to another place in 
India/return to his country to the SP 24 hrs in advance; 
7. The check-post of entry and exit and the mode of his travel are also 
specified on the visa and he has to seek permission for change in any of 
these. The check post of exit, if it is different from the checkpost of entry, 
informs the check-post of entry about the departure of the visa holder. 
Thus, all efforts are made to ensure that the Pak Nationals coming to the 
country on short-term visa go back to their country. Such of them who do not 
abide by the terms and conditions of visa are dealt with under the Foreigners Act 
for which powers have been delegated to the State Governments. The names of 
such nationals are put on the negative list. 
Driving licenses, ration cards, etc. are issued by the State Govts, after local 
verification of the particulars furnished by the applicant through the State police 
authorities. If a foreigner manages to acquire any of these documents by 
misrepresentation of facts, action is taken against him and he is deported back to his 
country for which powers have been delegated to the State Governments. The 
State Governments are regularly sensitised on the need to carefully scrutinize 
and verify all applications before issue of such documents.

2542. SHRI CM. IBRAHIM: Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether with a view to prioritizing hydro-electric power projects for 
speedy implementation basin-wise ranking studies have been carried out by the 
Central Electricity Authority; 
(b) if so, the details of the hydro-projects identified for prioritization, 
basin-wise; the power potential of each and the cost thereof; and 
(c) whether any new projects have been identified in the Krishna, Godavari and 
Cauveri basins, Bhima and Seena river basins, if so, the time frame 
contemplated for implementing the same? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRIMATI 
JAYAWANTI MEHTA): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The Government of India is 
according high priority to exploit the untapped hydro-electric potential in the 
country. In order to accelerate the process of survey and investigation of the new 
hydroelectric sites and to create a shelf of feasible projects which could be taken up 
for execution, the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) was asked to carry out a 
ranking study of the balance hydro sites for all the six river basins classified in 
the country. CEA has since brought out a Report on Preliminary Ranking Study 
of about 400 hydro schemes with an aggregate installed capacity of about 
1,07,000 MW which were identified but are yet to be developed. The inter-se-
prioritization of hydro sites within the basins has been carried out on

Steps for Making SGSY more Effective 
2546. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the objective of the Swamajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY); 
(b) whether these objectives have been fulfilled till date; 
(c) if so, the number of employment provided to the rural population 
through this scheme till date; and 
(d) the details of steps being taken to make this scheme more effective and 
productive? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) The objective of the Swamajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana 
(SGSY) is to bring the assisted poor families (swarozgaris) above the poverty line 
in three yean by providing them income-generating assets through a mix of 
bank credit and government subsidy. The assisted families, may be individuals 
or groups (Self Help Groups). However, the emphasis under the Scheme will 
be on Group Approach. 
(b) The SGSY is an on-going and process oriented Scheme. It may 
be, therefore, too early to say that  objectives of the Scheme have 
been fulfilled. The fact that 6.S8  lakhs Self Help Groups (SGHs) 
have been formed all over the Country, since inception of the 
Scheme, shows that the Scheme is progressing satisfactorily and on 
expected lines. 
(c) Since inception of the Scheme, till date, 22.76 lakhs 
Swarozgaries have been assisted fo r various economic activities with a 
total investment of Rs. 4290.79 Crores, involving Rs. 1424.19 Crores, 
as Subsidy and Rs. 2866.60 Crores as Credit from Banks. 
(d) Various steps being taken by the Ministry to make this Scheme 
more effective and productive includes, regular sensitisation of 
District and Field level functionaries and bankers, promotion of 
marketing of the SGSY products by participating in State, National 
and International exhibitions, regular inspection and verification of 
168 

[12 December, 2001]      RAJYA SABHA 
the Assets by Area officers under the Area officers Scheme, monitoring of the 
progress through Monthly, Quarterly, Half-yearly and Annual Periodical Reports, 
review of the Scheme by the Central level Coordination Committee and 
Performance Review Committee, Evaluation studies through reputed 
institutions/organisations, concurrent evaluations etc. An important step taken in 
this regard recently was holding of the National Conference on "Self Help 
Group Movement in the Country and the SGSY" at National Institute of 
Rural Development (NIRD), Hyderabad. The participants in the Conference 
included several Chief Ministers, Ministers of Rural Development from States, 
Senior Officials from Reserve Bank of India, NABARD, concerned 
Ministries, Departments and other agencies.

DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K. PATIL): (a) to (c) Under the 
Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP), funds are not allocated to the States, but 
are released to the Programme districts on project to project basis. A watershed 
development project taken up under the programme is required to be completed 
over a period of five years and funds are released for its completion in seven 
instalments. The first instalment is released along with the sanction of the project. 
Thereafter, each subsequent instalment is released on receipt of specific proposal

instalment is ensured at the time of release of subsequent instalment. Statement

structures, renovation of wells, gully control structures, diversion bunds, water 
delivery channels, contour bunding, road side plantation, tree plantation, live 
fencing, kitchen garden package, mango plantation, cashew plantation, mushroom 
cultivation, pasture development, etc.

New Scheme for total poverty-alleviation 
†2551. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: WiU the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have formulated any new ambitions scheme for 
total proverty alleviation; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI M. VENKAIAH 
NAIDU): (a) and (b) An ambitious Scheme namely the Sampooma Grameen 
Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) has been launched w.e.f. 25th September, 2001 to 
create additional wage employment with food security in the rural areas. 
There is, however, no scheme in the Ministry of Rural Development for total 
poverty alleviation. 
As regards the Sampooma Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY), the 
Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS) and the jawahar Gram Samridhi 
Yojana (JGSY) will get fully merged with the new Scheme. However, the 
EAS and JGSY will continue as a part of the new Scheme for the current 
year. Under the SGRY, 50 lakh tonnes of foodgrains amounting to Rs. 5000 
crores (at economic cost) will be provided every year, free of cost to the State 
Governments and Union Territory Administrations. The remaining funds 
(Rs. 5000 crores) will be utilized, to meet the cash component of wages and 
material cost. About 100 crores mandays of employment are envisaged to be 
generated every year in the rural areas through the SGRY.

Land Reforms as policy Instrument for Alleviation of Rural Poverty 
2563. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the Minister of RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Ninth Plan identified the land reforms as an 
important policy instrument for the alleviation of rural poverty; 
(b) if so, the progress report of the various States in this regard; 
(c) whether it is a fact that the Planning Commission has expressed unhappiness 
over the lack of progress in this regard in the midterm plan appraisal; and 
(d) if so, the reaction of Government and action proposed to be taken? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K. PATIL): (a) to (d) The 
schemes/activities undertaken towards land reforms have. br ought about a 
significant change in agrarian structure. 92% of the holdings in the country are now 
wholly-owned and self-operative. Ownership rights have been granted to 20 
million tillers and S.31 million acres of ceiling surplus land have been distributed 
to S.S4 million rural poor. Moreover, 14.75 million acres of Government 
Wastelands and 2.18 million acres of Bhoodanland have also been distributed 
among the eligible rural poor. 12.42 million tenants have their rights protected over 
an area of 15.63 million acres of land and 0.43 million acres of alienated land has 
been restored to STs. The Scheme of Computerisation of Land Records is being 
implemented in 569 districts of the country. 
The Planning Commission in its mid-term plan appraisal had observed that 
several factors had constrained the progress of Computerisation of Land Records 
such as delay in transfer of funds to the implementing authority by the State 
Governments, power shortages and delay in the construction of room with air 
conditioner for installation of computers and other equipments, delay in 
development of appropriate and comprehensive software as per requirement   of   
the   State   Governments,   delay   in   supply   and 
201 

RAJYA SABHA      [12 December, 2001] 
installation of the hardware, lack of adequate training facilities to staff to 
handle computers and non-availability of good vendors for taking up data 
entry work. 
With a view to speeding up the progress of the Scheme of 
Computerisation of Land Records, th e State Govts./UTs were impressed 
upon to take effective steps for tran sfer of funds to the implementing 
agencies in time and also to take up data entry work through private vendors 
so that the work could be completed within a specified time-frame. The State 
Govts /UTs have also been requested to procure and install hardware at the 
earliest and organise basic training programmes in order to train the Revenue 
Officials at the taluk level to facilitate speedy implementation of the Scheme.

Importing clothes on the basis of Export Quota by the US 
† 2569. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: 
                  SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH 'LALAN':  
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that even today the US is importing clothes on the 
basis of export quota fixed for the countries; 
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that the quota system has been causing a lot 
of hindrances in liberalisation policy of industry; and 
(c) if so, the reaction of Government  thereto and whether Government 
have urged upon the US to' do away with quota-system? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES (SHRI 
V. DHANANJAY KUMAR): (a) to (c) Textile imports in USA are governed by 
bilateral textile agreements entered into between India and other countries under the 
aegis of the Multi-Fibre Arrangement (MFA) which has since 1.1.1995, become 
part of the Agreement on Textiles & Clothing (ATC) contained in the Final Act of 
the Uruguay Round negotiations of the GATT. Quotas by themselves are trade 
restrictive. 
As per ATC, the textile quotas wo uld be phased out by 1st January 
2005.

2570. SHRI BRATIN SENGUP TA: Will the Minister of 
TEXTILES be pleased to state: 
(a) Whether the working group on Textiles and Jute Industry has recommended 
a uniform 8 per cent excise duty for the entire textile sector for next five years as 
a special dispensation; 
(b) If so, Government's reaction thereto; 
(c) Whether the total textile imports during the last fiscal year has increased 
substantially, but the exports were not increasing at the   • same rate; and 
(d) If so, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES (SHRI 
V. DHANANJAY KUMAR) (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The Working Group on 
Textile and Jute Industry for 10th Five Year Plan (2002—07) has recommended a 
number of measures to promote and develop the Indian Textile Industry for 
consideration of the Planning Commission. One of them is to broaden the tax 
net to link all states of textile production i.e. from fiber to the fabric stage by 
reducing the excise duty structure to a uniform level of 8 per cent.

year as against a decline of 25.2 per cent in total textile imports, in value

adequate availability of yarn packed in hank form for use in handlooms;

handloom sector to cope with the competition from other sectors.
